description: Acute bacterial disease caused by Bacillus anthracis, often associated with contaminated soil after heavy rains or excavation. Can cause sudden death with minimal warning. A zoonotic disease: never open a carcass or handle blood without protection.

Highly contagious viral disease of cloven-hoofed animals causing fever, vesicles on the mouth and feet, and severe production loss. Outbreaks spread rapidly through direct contact, contaminated feed, and movement of animals and people between farms.
aliases: foot and mouth disease;foot and mouth;foot mouth disease;fmd;foot-mouth disease

description: Viral disease transmitted by biting insects, characterized by fever and firm nodules on the skin. Affects cattle and buffalo, with economic impact from reduced milk production, weight loss, and secondary infections of skin lesions.
aliases: lumpy skin disease;lumpy skin;lumpy disease;lsd;lumpy chami;goli roga

description: Inflammation of the udder, usually caused by bacteria entering through the teat canal during milking or in unhygienic housing. Common in dairy cattle and buffalo; ranges from mild subclinical cases to severe toxic mastitis requiring urgent treatment.

Bacterial infection (Brucella) causing reproductive failure, abortion, and chronic illness in cattle and buffalo. Zoonotic: humans can contract it from aborted materials, raw milk, and infected animals.
